`xcrunner load` imports an image saved with `docker save`, and `uv pip install` works inside containers on hosts where only the udocker engine runs.

## Load an image saved with docker

An image that is in no registry, such as one built locally, can now be carried as a file to a host without docker, such as an HPC node:

    docker save myimage:1 -o myimage.tar                 # where docker has the image
    xcrunner load -i myimage.tar                         # on the host without docker

`xcrunner load` reads the archive `docker save` writes (Docker 25 or newer), plain or gzipped, from a file or standard input, and stores the image under the name the archive records. `--tag NAME:TAG` adds a name, and is needed when the archive records none. A file holding several images is refused: save one image per file. `xcrunner docker load` and `docker image load` through the docker shim do the same.

## uv under udocker

On login nodes and other hosts that block user namespaces and ptrace, xcrunner runs images through udocker's Fakechroot mode. There, every `uv pip install` of a package not already in the image failed with "Could not persist temporary file `/root/.cache/uv/…` … Permission denied (os error 13)". coala-runtime installs its Python packages with uv, so h5py, llvmlite and others could not be installed.

Fakechroot maps the paths a program passes to the C library. uv persists each cache lock with a raw `renameat2` system call (the `tempfile` crate, through `rustix`), which skips the C library. With `HOME=/root`, that rename reached the host's `/root`, which only root can write. Pointing `UV_CACHE_DIR` at a folder that exists only inside the container fails the same way, with "No such file or directory".

Containers run under udocker now get `UV_CACHE_DIR` set to a shared `.udocker-uv-cache` folder next to the containers, mounted at the same path inside, so the mapped calls and the raw rename reach the same folder. The cache is shared, so later containers reuse downloaded wheels. A `UV_CACHE_DIR` you set yourself is kept. The README lists this under the udocker limits.
